the hospitality management research has changed over the past twenty years, with a greater focus on quantitative research, a move away from the use of secondary data, a focus on global issues, and an increasing interest in the use of new technology.

the use of the Internet has become an important part of hospitality management research, that hospitality management research has become much more global and international in its scope, and that the research has become more complex and challenging.
the hospitality research is changing and that the changes are related to the changes in the industry.

the human experience of hospitality.
the management of people and the management of places.
the development of knowledge, and the application of that knowledge, to the benefit of our industry and society.

there are no trends in hospitality research, but rather a constant stream of research topics and issues, and the challenge is for researchers to be able to identify and select those that are of interest to them, and that are of interest in the context of hospitality management.

the field is healthy and vibrant, with a strong and growing body of research, with a good balance between conceptual and empirical work, and with an increasing number of researchers and publications in the field.
there has been a significant change in the nature and direction of hospitality research since 1993, and this is likely to continue.

we have seen a move away from descriptive research to a much greater emphasis on quantitative studies.
the hospitality industry and its research have changed and will continue to change in ways that are difficult to anticipate.
the hospitality industry has changed and so has the research agenda.

the hospitality industry is in the midst of a transformation that is changing the very nature of hospitality and the role of the hotel.
we need to continue to focus on the needs of hospitality managers and practitioners and the challenges they face.
